mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has surged 39.7% in t-1w and remains elevated at 16.6% in t-0w, indicating sustained outdoor recreation substitution for indoor retail. This substitution effect will persist over the next four weeks, suppressing RETAIL_REC recovery below its four-week baseline mean.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days exceeds the mean of the prior 28 days, or PARKS mobility falls below 5% in any of the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has stabilized near baseline (1.9% in t-0w) after volatility, signaling normalized essential-goods purchasing behavior. This normalization removes the substitution pressure on RETAIL_REC, allowing retail-and-recreation to recover toward baseline over the next two weeks as confidence in non-essential shopping returns.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains within ±5% of baseline for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM at 1.9% in t-0w after -3.1% in t-2w
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM deviates beyond ±10% from baseline in the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC fails to increase from its t-0w level of -23.4%.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT stations remain severely depressed (-29.1% in t-0w), constraining commuter access to retail districts. The persistent transit deficit directly limits RETAIL_REC recovery because foot traffic to shopping venues depends on transit connectivity. RETAIL_REC will remain suppressed as long as TRANSIT stays below -25%.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -25% for three consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -29.1% in t-0w, -28.4% in t-1w, -37.7% in t-2w
failure_condition: TRANSIT rises above -20% in any of the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC increases by more than 5 percentage points despite TRANSIT remaining below -25%.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has stabilized around -16.6% (t-0w), indicating a floor in remote-work adoption. Combined with RESIDENTIAL stabilization at 6.6%, this signals that the population is no longer shifting toward home-based activity. The cessation of this shift removes downward pressure on RETAIL_REC, enabling recovery over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES variance t-2w to t-0w is 6.8 pp
fact:RESIDENTIAL variance t-2w to t-0w is 2.7 pp
failure_condition: WORKPLACES falls below -20% or RESIDENTIAL rises above 8% in any of the next two weeks, indicating renewed shift away from workplaces.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has improved from -35.7% (t-3w) to -23.4% (t-0w), a 12.3 pp recovery trend. If this linear recovery rate persists, RETAIL_REC will reach approximately -11% by week t+4w, representing a net positive direction relative to the four-week baseline mean of -28.5%. The mechanism assumes policy constraints are gradually easing.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC improves by at least 3 pp week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 12.3 pp over three weeks (t-3w to t-0w)
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines by more than 2 pp in any of the next two weeks, or the four-week mean of RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than -28.5%.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility spike (39.7% in t-1w, 16.6% in t-0w) combined with RESIDENTIAL stabilization (6.6% in t-0w) indicates a seasonal shift toward outdoor leisure. This seasonal pattern typically precedes a rebalancing toward indoor retail as weather normalizes or seasonal events conclude. RETAIL_REC will recover within one week as the outdoor-leisure peak exhausts.
candidate_trigger: PARKS exceeds 15% while RESIDENTIAL remains below 8%
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at 16.6% and RESIDENTIAL at 6.6% in t-0w
failure_condition: PARKS remains above 15% for more than two consecutive weeks, or RETAIL_REC fails to increase in week t+1w.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT depression (-29.1%) and WORKPLACES depression (-16.6%) interact to create a low-mobility regime where commuting and transit-dependent retail access are both suppressed. This dual suppression will persist over the next four weeks unless both series improve simultaneously. RETAIL_REC will remain below -20% as long as this interaction persists.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT below -25% AND WORKPLACES below -15% simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:Both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain depressed in t-0w
failure_condition: Either TRANSIT rises above -20% or WORKPLACES rises above -10% in the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC increases by more than 3 pp despite both remaining in the suppression regime.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM volatility (ranging from -3.1% to 4.6% across t-2w to t-1w) reflects uncertainty in essential-goods purchasing patterns. When GROCERY_PHARM stabilizes within ±3% of baseline, it signals consumer confidence recovery. This confidence will extend to discretionary retail within two weeks, driving RETAIL_REC upward as consumers resume non-essential shopping.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM variance over two weeks falls below 2 pp
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM variance t-1w to t-0w is 2.7 pp
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM variance exceeds 3 pp in the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC fails to increase by at least 2 pp in week t+2w.
